## Purpose and entry points
OpenPose is a C++ real-time human keypoint-estimation library: multi-person 2D body/foot, hand, and face inference, with optional tracking, calibration, and multi-camera 3D reconstruction. The CLI demo is `examples/openpose/openpose.cpp`; public C++ integration centers on `include/openpose/wrapper/wrapper.hpp`; Python bindings are implemented in `python/openpose/openpose_python.cpp`. Build orchestration begins at `CMakeLists.txt`.

## Wrapper and pipeline orchestration
The Wrapper API assembles configured worker stages from command-line flags or API structs, manages synchronous/asynchronous execution, and exposes extension points for custom input, preprocessing, postprocessing, and output. `Datum` is the unit flowing through the pipeline, carrying images, keypoints, heatmaps, and metadata.
- `include/openpose/wrapper/wrapper.hpp`
- `src/openpose/wrapper/wrapperAuxiliary.cpp`
- `include/openpose/core/datum.hpp`

## Input acquisition and threading boundary
Producer implementations normalize image directories, video files/capture, webcams, IP cameras, and FLIR/Point Grey cameras into `Datum`s. A generic worker/queue/thread framework isolates stages, supports ordered processing, and enables parallel/asynchronous pipelines.
- `src/openpose/producer/producer.cpp`
- `src/openpose/producer/flirReader.cpp`
- `include/openpose/thread/threadManager.hpp`

## Pose inference and keypoint assembly
The pose subsystem selects body models and drives network extraction. Caffe-backed network execution produces heatmaps/part-affinity fields; net stages find peaks (NMS), resize/merge outputs, and connect body parts into per-person skeletons. OpenCV network support is also present.
- `src/openpose/pose/poseExtractorCaffe.cpp`
- `src/openpose/net/netCaffe.cpp`
- `src/openpose/net/bodyPartConnectorBase.cpp`

## Face and hand refinement
After body detection, face and hand modules derive regions of interest, run dedicated Caffe models per detected person, and attach refined landmarks to the shared datum. This is a deliberate dependency boundary: body pose can run alone, while face/hand are optional follow-on inference workloads.
- `src/openpose/face/faceExtractorCaffe.cpp`
- `src/openpose/hand/handExtractorCaffe.cpp`
- `src/openpose/hand/handDetector.cpp`

## Rendering, output, and external consumers
CPU/GPU renderers overlay body, face, and hand results. Output workers serialize keypoints/heatmaps, images/video, BVH, COCO JSON, or transmit results via UDP; GUI workers display 2D/3D visualization. The Unity binding provides a separate integration surface.
- `src/openpose/pose/poseGpuRenderer.cpp`
- `src/openpose/filestream/peopleJsonSaver.cpp`
- `src/openpose/filestream/udpSender.cpp`

## 3D, calibration, and tracking extensions
The calibration module estimates camera parameters; the 3D module reads them and triangulates synchronized multi-view poses, with joint-angle estimation available. Tracking assigns persistent person IDs and uses pyramidal Lucas–Kanade support, primarily for single-person smoothing/speedup.
- `src/openpose/calibration/cameraParameterEstimation.cpp`
- `src/openpose/3d/poseTriangulation.cpp`
- `src/openpose/tracking/personTracker.cpp`

## Runtime and dependency model
CMake builds the library, examples, and optional Python module across CPU, CUDA, and OpenCL paths. Core external dependencies are Caffe (inference), OpenCV (vision/I/O), CUDA/cuDNN where enabled, and optional Spinnaker for FLIR cameras; model definitions reside under `models/` and weights are fetched by scripts.
- `cmake/Modules/FindCaffe.cmake`
- `src/openpose/gpu/cuda.cu`
- `cmake/Modules/FindSpinnaker.cmake`
